lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we round a number to the nearest ten, we find the closest multiple of ten to our number.

Content:
For example, let's round the following number to the nearest ten:

Content:
[MATH: 123]

Content:
We begin by drawing a number line:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/06e39b40e30aa2a316706e96408b3759]

Content:
Looking at the number line, the closest multiples of ten to [MATH: 123] are [MATH: 120] and [MATH: 130.]

Content:
Let's add these multiples of [MATH: 10] to our diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/91b395cc6c2dc3175b739bf0ccd7fdec]

Content:
Now, since [MATH: 123] is closer to [MATH: {\color{DarkGreen}120}] than [MATH: {\color{SaddleBrown}130},] this is the number we round to.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/012cd45d227b8acaa6bd859add718e63]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 123] rounded to the nearest ten is [MATH: 120.]

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: Recognizing Multiples of 10 and 100

Content:
We can use the following rules to recognize multiples of [MATH: 10] and [MATH: 100{:}]

Content:
- Multiples of [MATH: 10] always end in at least one zero.

For example, all the following numbers are multiples of [MATH: 10{:}]
[MATH: 20, \qquad 80, \qquad 110, \qquad 200]

Content:
- Similarly, multiples of [MATH: 100] always end in at least two zeros.

For example, all the following numbers are multiples of [MATH: 100{:}]
[MATH: 100, \qquad 500, \qquad 2,100, \qquad 3,000]

Content:
Let's look at an example of rounding up to the nearest [MATH: 100.]

---

Item 3 — Example: Rounding Down Using a Number Line

Example Prompt:
Using the number line below, round [MATH: 4,335] to the nearest hundred.

[IMG: /graphics/4c3f5e39721132595827693759a8a2e6]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Rounding a number to the nearest hundred means finding the closest multiple of one hundred to our number.

The closest multiples of [MATH: 100] to [MATH: 4,335] are [MATH: 4,300] and [MATH: 4,400.]

Let's add these multiples of [MATH: 100] to our diagram.

[IMG: /graphics/61022c44571b4faa1f51b68316888bf7]

Since [MATH: 4,335] is closer to [MATH: {\color{DarkGreen}4,300}] than [MATH: {\color{SaddleBrown}4,400},] this is the number we round to.

[IMG: /graphics/fb6d37094a500c7c8c89b72320a64180]

Therefore, [MATH: 4,335] rounded to the nearest hundred is [MATH: 4,300.]

Item 6 — Tutorial: Rounding Down Whole Numbers Using Place Value Charts

Content:
We can round whole numbers using a place value chart.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's again round the following number to the nearest ten:

Content:
[MATH: 123]

Content:
We start by writing our number's digits in a place value chart. Since we're rounding to the nearest ten, we highlight the tens place:

Content:
| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] |

Content:
We then look one digit to the right in the chart (i.e., the ones place) and compare it to the number [MATH: 5{:}]

Content:
| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red}3}] |

Content:
Since [MATH: \color{red}3] is less than [MATH: 5], we round down. To do this, we put [MATH: \color{blue}0] in the ones place:

Content:
| hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}] |

Content:
And that's it!

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: 123] rounded to the nearest ten is [MATH: 120.]

---

Item 7 — Example: Rounding Down to the Nearest Ten

Example Prompt:
Round [MATH: 25,234] to the nearest ten.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We start by writing our number into a place value chart. Notice the tens place:

| ten-thousands | thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 4] |

We then look one digit to the right in the chart (this will be the ones place) and compare it to the number [MATH: 5{:}]

| ten-thousands | thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red}4}] |

Since [MATH: \color{red}4] is less than [MATH: 5], we round down. To do this, we put [MATH: \color{blue}0] in the ones place:

| ten-thousands | thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}] |

Therefore, [MATH: 25,234] rounded to the nearest ten is [MATH: 25,230.]

Item 10 — Tutorial: Rounding Down to Other Value Places

Content:
We can use a similar method to round whole numbers to the nearest hundred, thousand, ten-thousand, and so on.

Content:
For example, let's round [MATH: 1,824] to the nearest hundred.

Content:
We start by writing our number into a place value chart. But this time, since we're rounding to the nearest hundred, we highlight the hundreds place:

Content:
| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 4] |

Content:
We then look one digit to the right in the chart (this will be the tens place) and compare it to the number [MATH: 5{:}]

Content:
| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red}2}] | [MATH: 4] |

Content:
Since [MATH: \color{red}2] is less than [MATH: 5], we round down. To do this, we put [MATH: \color{blue}0] in all places to the right of the hundreds (both tens and ones):

Content:
| thousands | hundreds | tens | ones |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}] | [MATH: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}] |

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 1,824] rounded to the nearest hundred is [MATH: 1,800.]

---
